cards.text: Paul is writing to the believers in Colossae (Colossians 1:1-2), and he's already spent a long time telling them who Christ is (Colossians 1:15-20). Now he hits them with a "Therefore." Baker, when Paul says therefore, you put the cookie DOWN, because here comes the part where you actually DO something.

cards.question: Paul reminds the Colossians that they received Christ Jesus as Lord. What does he tell them to do now?

cards.text: Then Paul piles on the pictures: rooted and built up in Him. A tree with roots and a building going up, all in one breath.

cards.question: Paul tells the Colossians to stay established in the faith just as they were taught.

cards.text: And Paul tops it off with one more: overflowing with thankfulness. Roots, walls, and now a FLOOD of thanks, friend, Paul does NOT do small.

Then Paul gets serious: don't let anyone take you captive through philosophy and empty deception, based on human tradition and the spiritual forces of the world. Baker, I spent YEARS stuck in the back of a junk drawer, so trust me, captive is NOT where you want to end up.

cards.question: Paul says this philosophy and empty deception is based on human tradition and the spiritual forces of the world rather than on ___.
So why hold on to Christ instead of some clever philosophy? According to Paul, how much of the fullness of the Deity dwells in Christ?

cards.text: All of it, dwelling in bodily form. Baker, when you've already got ALL of it, there is nowhere else to shop.

cards.question: Paul tells the Colossians they still need something more than Christ to be complete.
The Colossians have been made complete in Christ. Paul says Christ is the head over whom?

cards.text: Next Paul brings up circumcision, the sign of God's covenant with Abraham (Genesis 17:11). And he tells these believers that in Him, they were circumcised too.

cards.question: Paul says this circumcision of the Colossians was performed by ___.
This circumcision wasn't done by human hands. What does Paul say got put off in it?

cards.text: Then Paul paints another picture: in baptism, they were buried with Him. Baker, I spent YEARS buried under takeout menus, so trust me, how this one ends matters.

cards.question: The Colossians were buried with Christ in baptism. What does Paul say happened next?

answers.text: They waited for Him to return
They were sent out to find Him

cards.question: Paul says the Colossians were raised with Christ through their faith in the power of God, who raised Him from the dead.

cards.text: Then Paul looks back at where they started: dead in their trespasses and in the uncircumcision of their sinful nature. Not hit-the-snooze-four-times tired, friend, DEAD.

cards.question: The Colossians were dead in their trespasses. What does Paul say God did?

answers.text: Gave them rules to fix it
Waited for them to wake up

cards.question: Paul says God forgave us ___ our trespasses.

cards.text: Did you catch that? Paul just switched from "you" to "us," so he's counting himself in on that forgiveness too.
Then Paul talks about a debt ascribed to us in the decrees that stood against us. Friend, you know that bill with your name on it in BOLD, just sitting there staring at you?

cards.question: Paul says God canceled the debt that stood against us.
God took that debt away, nailing it to the ___.

cards.text: That debt is GONE, nailed to the cross, and Paul's not even done. Next he turns to the powers and authorities.

cards.question: What does Paul say was done to the powers and authorities?
Paul says the powers and authorities were beaten quietly, somewhere nobody could see.

cards.text: Nope. He made a public spectacle of them, triumphing over them by the cross, and friend, that's the final score lit up on the stadium screen for EVERYBODY to see.

findings.problem: The joke 'when you've already got ALL of it, there is nowhere else to shop' tells the baker they need nothing beyond Christ. That gives away the answer to card 10, which asks whether the Colossians still need something more than Christ to be complete (Colossians 2:10).

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: A baker could argue the wrong answers are right. Christ is head of the church (Colossians 1:18), so 'Every elder and deacon' and 'Every priest and prophet' could be argued to fall under 'every ruler and authority.' Replace them with wrong answers that are clearly not true of Christ's headship.

rule.text: No near-matches. A wrong answer never means the same as the right answer, or close to it. If a baker could argue it's right, replace it.

findings.problem: 'This circumcision of the Colossians' points back to story card 1, which is no longer on screen. The question doesn't say which circumcision is meant: the one Paul says they received in Him.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: 'God took that debt away' points back to card 12 with 'that debt.' The question doesn't say what the debt is: the debt ascribed to us in the decrees that stood against us.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: This card reuses the joke from stop 1 card 6 almost word for word: 'Baker, I spent YEARS [in the junk drawer], so trust me, ...'. The second use ('how this one ends matters') also lands softer than a laugh.
findings.question: Is Papa Dorin allowed to repeat the same joke setup within one walkthrough, or should each joke be fresh? The docs say 'No formula' and 'push it further,' but they don't speak to reusing a joke structure.
